meta.tagline: Bitcoin and Lightning on your own device
meta.description: Illustrated guide to the DFX BTC Taro Wallet: create a wallet, receive and send bitcoin, secure your backup, use Lightning.

chapters.title: Getting started
chapters.summary: Open the app for the first time and create a wallet.
chapters.intro: On first launch the app creates a wallet on your device. The keys stay on the phone — DFX has no access to them and cannot restore a lost wallet. That is why the disclaimer comes first, and why the next step after creating a wallet is always the backup.

chapters.title: Receiving bitcoin
chapters.summary: Show a receiving address and accept a payment.
chapters.intro: To receive, the wallet shows an address as a QR code. Whoever pays scans that code. Amount and description are optional and only help you recognise the payment later. The wallet creates a new address for every payment — that is intended and good for your privacy.

chapters.title: Sending bitcoin
chapters.summary: Make a payment, usually via the QR scanner.
chapters.intro: Sending requires the recipient's address. The scanner is the easiest way: it reads the other party's QR code and fills in address and amount by itself. A sent bitcoin payment cannot be recalled — so check address and amount once more before confirming.

chapters.title: Backup and security
chapters.summary: Secure the recovery phrase and export the wallet.
chapters.intro: The twelve-word recovery phrase is the wallet. Whoever holds it holds the money; whoever loses it and loses the device has lost the money. It belongs on paper in a safe place — not in a photo, not in a chat, not in the cloud. In this chapter the phrase and the export QR are redacted, because otherwise they would sit publicly in the repository.

chapters.title: Lightning
chapters.summary: Small amounts, instantly and at very low cost.
chapters.intro: Lightning is a second layer on top of Bitcoin for small, fast payments. The Lightning wallet in this app runs through a provider (LNDHub) — lightning.space is preselected, DFX.swiss can be chosen as well. Unlike the on-chain wallet, the balance is held by that provider; for larger amounts the on-chain wallet is the right place.

chapters.title: More wallets: adding and importing
chapters.summary: Multi-device wallet, an extra Lightning wallet, importing an existing wallet.
chapters.intro: Besides the wallet from first launch you can add more: a multi-device wallet spread across three devices, where two of them must approve every payment, or another Lightning wallet. A wallet created elsewhere can be imported from a recovery phrase, a private key or a QR code.

chapters.title: Settings
chapters.summary: Currency, language, security, network and tools.
chapters.intro: The settings let you change the display currency and the language, lock the app, and switch the Electrum server in use. The tools are meant for rare occasions — for instance to check whether an address belongs to your own wallet.
